- scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  Line or code reference: kill-switch arm — `if [ "${CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED:-true}" != "true" ]; then _mu_unhandled_reason="disabled"; fi`
  PROBLEM: The kill switch's effective meaning has changed in a way the README does not spell out at the variable level. Previously `CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED=false` skipped the union block and let the Codex resolver run the manifest conflict; now it enters the block, sets `_mu_unhandled_reason="disabled"`, and exits 1 with the new diagnostic. Operators who set the switch to opt back into the model resolver will instead see a hard fail-closed.
  WHY: Any consumer repo that flipped the kill switch to bypass a bug in the set-algebra arm, or that simply treats `false` as "let the resolver have it", will now get `::error::Manifest union-merge: unhandled reason=disabled` instead of a resolver run. The behavior change is documented in the README/agents.md tables and the changelog fragment, but the variable's own docstring-level description still reads like a soft kill switch, and nothing in the new diagnostic tells the operator that "false" used to mean "fall through". This is the same concern the fix constraints flag ("never rename or remove existing identifiers"); the name is preserved but the semantics of `false` shifted from "skip the feature" to "fail the prepare step". The strict `!= "true"` test also treats values like `yes` or `1` as disabled, which is consistent with the rest of the repo but worth noting because the diagnostic will report `CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED=yes` while still claiming the feature is disabled.
- scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  Line or code reference: integration-sync arm — `orchestrator/project-*) echo "Manifest union-merge: skipped on integration-sync branch ..."; _mu_unhandled_reason="integration_sync"`
  PROBLEM: Pre-fix, integration-sync branches on a `manifest`-only conflict were routed to the Codex resolver (`CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED=true` path that hit the integration-sync case simply logged and continued). Post-fix, the same branch now exits 1, which means every active orchestrator project whose integration branch is ahead of `main` will trip the deterministic fail-closed the first time its manifest re-baselines against a moved `main`. The previous "skip on integration-sync" carve-out is gone.
  WHY: For an orchestrator project mid-wave that has been appending changelog fragments to `.ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt` on each sub-issue squash, the next `main` -> `orchestrator/project-N` sync that conflicts on the manifest will no longer reach the resolver — preparation will fail closed, the integration self-heal will burn `INTEGRATION_SYNC_CONFLICT_MAX_RETRIES`, and the integration judge path takes over. The heal issue acknowledges this is intentional ("Integration-sync branches are excluded because later fingerprint expansion may widen the resolver working set"), and the changelog + agents.md + README all call it out, so it is documented; the concern is purely operational: the impact on currently-active orchestrator projects is asymmetric with the previous carve-out and the plan/migration story for in-flight projects is not spelled out in the changelog fragment.
- agents.md / README.md / changelog.d/6608-manifest-modify-delete-conflict.md | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Line or code reference: `CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED` row in both env-var tables; the `## AGENTS.md` row in agents.md; the changelog fragment prose
  PROBLEM: The variable name is preserved (per §6), but the meaning of `CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED=false` has shifted from "skip this step, let the resolver try" to "fail preparation with a `disabled` diagnostic". The README row and the changelog fragment both describe the new behavior accurately but neither explicitly says "the previous `false` meaning of `let the resolver handle it` no longer applies". A repo that pinned `false` to work around an earlier bug will silently start failing preparation on every manifest conflict.
  WHY: Operators reading the row may assume a kill switch still maps to "off = resolver path". The new behavior is fail-closed even when the operator opted out. The changelog text and agents.md row both convey the change, but the variable row in the README does not call out the meaning shift at the variable level; consider adding a "previously `false` meant ..." clause to the row so a grep for the variable surfaces the semantic change. This is documentation hygiene, not a code bug.

  File: scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh
  Location: end of the kill-switch arm, after `_mu_unhandled_reason="disabled"` (around the `echo "::error::... CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED=${CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED:-true}; ..."` line)
  Issue: The diagnostic includes the raw env-var name but not the previous meaning. When an operator sees `reason=disabled` they may assume the kill switch was the right thing to flip, when the new behavior is that flipping it now hard-fails the run.
  Suggested minimal fix: append `; set CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED=true to enable safe deterministic resolution` (or equivalent operator-facing pointer) to the diagnostic line. ~1 line changed.
